title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — July 2026
description: This week, we're looking at the IPO from Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited. We'll learn what an IPO is and why companies offer them to the public.

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's net banking portal using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, or through your stockbroker's platform.
The lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer shares than the specified lot size.
A Demat account is an electronic account that holds your shares and other securities in a digital format, similar to how a bank account holds your money.
An IPO is oversubscribed when the total number of shares applied for by investors is more than the total number of shares the company is offering.

faq.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary markets?
faq.a: The primary market is where new securities are issued for the first time (like an IPO). The secondary market is where existing securities are traded among investors (like buying and selling shares on the stock exchange after listing).
